_meta.what: 手写补充词典：六档词表与 build_general_dict.py 生成的补充词典都漏收的常用词
_meta.why: 2026-10-15 用户导入《A Piece of Red Calico》后反馈「生词表有的行音标/词性/释义全空」。追下来发现 calico 这类常用词在 vendor/english-vocabulary-master 的 11.7 万条源数据里根本不存在，六档索引和补充词典都查不到，生词表里就留下三列全空的一行。
_meta.provenance: 本文件每一条都是**手写**的，不是从任何开源词库拷贝而来。上游数据源（KyleBing/english-vocabulary-master，MIT）已确认不含这些词；为避免「编一个没有出处的释义」，这里如实标注 src=hand。音标为通用 IPA，词性与释义按常用义项。
_meta.how_measured: 种子清单由 scripts/probe_missing_words.py 量出：测 505 个常用词，456 个有词条、49 个完全查不到，本文件补的就是那 49 个（去掉探针里的一个拼写错误 desereter）。
_meta.format: 与 data/dict/general.json 完全一致：{word: {p 音标, pos 词性, t 释义, e 英释, s 例句}}，便于同一套加载代码复用。
_meta.caution: 以后新增条目请保持「确实是常用词、且确认六档与 general.json 都没有」——不要把这个文件变成又一个来路不明的词库。

almsgiving.e: the practice of giving money or goods to poor people
almsgiving.s: The monastery survived on the almsgiving of neighbouring farms.

beauteous.t: 美丽的；美好的（文学用词）
beauteous.e: beautiful, especially in a literary or poetic way
beauteous.s: He wrote a beauteous line about the harbour at dawn.

bier.e: a stand on which a coffin rests before burial
bier.s: The bier was carried slowly through the narrow lane.

broth.e: thin soup made by stewing meat, fish or vegetables in water
broth.s: She warmed the broth and added a handful of herbs.

buoy.e: a floating mark used to guide ships or mark a channel
buoy.s: A red buoy marked the edge of the shallow water.

byway.e: a minor or little-used road, away from the main route
byway.s: They turned off the highway onto a grassy byway.

calico.e: a plain white cotton cloth, or one printed with a pattern
calico.s: She cut a piece of red calico and held it against the light.

calicoes.t: calico 的复数：印花棉布；白布
calicoes.s: The shop sold calicoes of every shade of red and blue.

cask.e: a large barrel used for storing liquids, especially ale or wine
cask.s: The cask was tapped and the ale ran golden into the jugs.

centaur.e: a creature from Greek myth with a man's head and torso and a horse's body
centaur.s: The centaur is a familiar figure in Greek mythology.

coachman.e: a man who drives a horse-drawn coach
coachman.s: The coachman cracked his whip and the horses leaned forward.

convent.e: a community of nuns living under religious vows
convent.s: She was sent to the convent at the age of sixteen.

cortege.e: a solemn procession, especially at a funeral
cortege.s: The cortege moved quietly through the wet streets.

crib.e: a baby's bed with high sides; also a manger for animals
crib.s: The baby slept soundly in its crib by the fire.

crumpet.e: a thick soft British cake, toasted and buttered
crumpet.s: He ate a buttered crumpet with his morning tea.

damask.e: a rich woven fabric with a pattern visible on both sides
damask.s: The table was covered with white damask.

deserter.e: a person who leaves the armed forces without permission
deserter.s: The deserter was caught a mile from the camp.

distillery.e: a factory where spirits are produced by distillation
distillery.s: The old distillery still smells of malt and peat.

dyer.e: a person whose job is dyeing cloth or yarn
dyer.s: The dyer dipped the silk and it came out a deep red.

galoshes.e: waterproof overshoes, usually made of rubber
galoshes.s: He pulled on his galoshes before stepping into the slush.

gewgaw.t: 廉价小饰物；华而不实之物
gewgaw.s: The stall was piled with gewgaws nobody needed.

gibbet.e: a gallows, or a post on which executed bodies were hung as a warning
gibbet.s: The gibbet stood on the hill as a warning to travellers.

inglenook.e: a recess beside a fireplace, often with seats
inglenook.s: The cat slept in the inglenook all afternoon.

inkwell.e: a small container for holding writing ink
inkwell.s: He dipped the pen into the inkwell and hesitated.

kerb.e: the stone edge of a pavement (BrE; AmE curb)
kerb.s: The car mounted the kerb and stopped against a lamppost.

larder.e: a cool place where food is stored in a house
larder.s: There was cheese and cold meat in the larder.

lent.e: the period of fasting and penitence before Easter
lent.s: He gave up sugar for the whole of Lent.

lorgnette.e: eyeglasses held to the eyes by a long handle
lorgnette.s: She raised her lorgnette and studied him in silence.

milliner.e: a person who makes or sells women's hats
milliner.s: The milliner showed her a hat trimmed with velvet.

minotaur.t: 弥诺陶洛斯（希腊神话牛头怪）
minotaur.e: the bull-headed monster of Greek legend kept in the Labyrinth
minotaur.s: Theseus killed the Minotaur and found his way out.

muslin.e: a light, loosely woven cotton fabric
muslin.s: The curtains were of plain white muslin.

nave.e: the central part of a church, where the congregation sits
nave.s: Light fell through the high windows of the nave.

portmanteau.e: a large travelling case, typically made of leather
portmanteau.s: He packed a portmanteau and left before dawn.

repast.e: a meal, especially a formal or substantial one
repast.s: After the repast the guests moved to the drawing-room.

scone.e: a small soft British cake, often eaten with cream and jam
scone.s: She baked scones for the afternoon tea.

scullery.e: a small room next to a kitchen, for washing dishes
scullery.s: The pans were stacked in the scullery.

silo.e: a tall tower for storing grain or silage
silo.s: The concrete silo stood above the barley fields.

solstice.e: either of the two times of year when the sun is furthest from the equator
solstice.s: The festival is held at the summer solstice.

tithe.t: 什一税；（交给教会的）十分之一
tithe.e: one tenth of a person's income, paid to the church
tithe.s: Every farmer was expected to pay a tithe on his corn.

truffle.e: a strong-smelling underground fungus used as a delicacy
truffle.s: The chef shaved black truffle over the eggs.

tun.e: a large cask for beer, wine or spirits
tun.s: A tun of wine was rolled into the cellar.

unlovely.e: not attractive or pleasing to look at
unlovely.s: The house was unlovely but warm and dry.

unmindful.e: not conscious or aware of something; heedless
unmindful.s: He rode on, unmindful of the coming storm.

unroll.e: to open or spread out something that was rolled up
unroll.s: She unrolled the map across the table.

vat.e: a large tank or tub used for holding liquids
vat.s: The cloth was lowered into a vat of dark dye.

vellum.e: fine parchment made from calfskin, used for manuscripts
vellum.s: The manuscript was copied onto vellum.

victuals.s: They carried enough victuals for a fortnight.

yardarm.e: the outer end of a yard on a square-rigged ship
yardarm.s: A sailor climbed out along the yardarm to furl the sail.

yule.e: the Christmas season, especially in older or poetic use
yule.s: The old songs still speak of the yule log.
